newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM says party may leave govt over pensions.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM says party may leave govt over pensions.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Thursday his ruling Civic Democratic Party (ODS) would pull out of the governing coalition if an opposition plan to lower the official retirement age was approved by parliament.

"Currently, laws are in play whose approval we would interpret as a basic threat to the very basics of the transformation -- not only economic, but also social and in health care -- as something in which we could no longer participate, and we would have to leave the government," Klaus said in a statement issued by his party.

The statement said that steps by a coalition partner, the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL), to push through its candidate as chairman in the Senate and to vote with the opposition on a new pension proposal had violated the agreement which formed the coalition and the minority government.

The largest opposition party, the Social Democrats, recently approved in the first of three required readings in parliament a proposal which would lower the retirement age to 60 years for men and to 53 to 57 years for women, replacing a government plan to gradually raise the pension age.

Klaus's government, before losing its majority in the lower house of parliament in June, had approved the plan to raise the retirement age as a way to head off an expected crisis in financing pensions in the long term.

In the statement Klaus's right-wing ODS also objected to a Social Democrat plan which would strengthen state intervention to help support the agriculture sector, and said if this proposal was approved it would also be "unbearable".
